business_summary.headline: A calm day overall: every recent fix is still holding, a fresh version of the website went live smoothly with zero errors, and a long-standing newsletter mystery finally got solved (good news: it wasn't a bug). The one real carryover issue — a handful of destination pages not showing the right 'not found' response — is still unfixed and was double-checked again today. One small new item: a recent email newsletter reached fewer people than expected, worth a quick look.
context: This is one in a running series of daily, fully-automated health checks of nakshiq.com that has been going since early May 2026 — every check in this report was performed live against the real site today, not estimated or carried over from a prior day.
There was no automated check run yesterday (September 6th) — today's check compares against the results from two days ago (September 5th) instead of one.

A new version of the website went live sometime between yesterday and today. Every check performed after that update came back clean — no errors, all pages loading correctly — which is a good sign for that update.
traffic_lights: All 32 core pages checked loaded successfully; 10/10 sampled destination pages loaded correctly in both English and Hindi, even right after a fresh website update.
Still working correctly on all three places on the site that show a map — confirmed again today on an actual randomly-sampled destination page.
Zero server errors of any signature found in the last 2 days, spanning both the update and today's checks.
Still fixed. The site's structured data and on-page counters continue to show the correct, current destination count.
All sampled pages show correct Hindi language tags, titles, and section headings. The one known, narrower gap (main heading in English on a subset of pages) continues unchanged — not urgent.
Every one of the 533 destinations has emergency contact info on file, well above the safety minimum. No change.
The file search engines use to discover pages remains complete: roughly 25,000 URLs covering all 533 destinations.

The overnight job that keeps hotel and stay recommendations current ran successfully again, and this time it also caught and correctly avoided two cases of geographically wrong recommendations rather than publishing them — a good sign the built-in safety checks work as designed.

Resolved today: the subscriber who appeared to never receive the first newsletter had actually unsubscribed on their own a few days after it was sent. Not a technical problem. The most recent newsletter send (Sept 6) delivered cleanly to everyone it was sent to.

Still not fixed: a small number of destination pages that share their name with an Indian state (Puducherry, Goa, Sikkim, Delhi, Chandigarh) show the wrong technical response for nonsense web addresses. Directly re-tested today and confirmed unchanged. Not visible to search engines or a normal visitor, but still worth a developer fix.

The recurring pattern of a daily analytics report file not being automatically saved to the project's permanent history happened again today, in a smaller, simpler form than before. This check saved it, but a technical limitation in today's checking environment meant the save couldn't be fully finished without a follow-up step — same as several prior days.
New today, low priority: the most recent newsletter send reached only 8 out of 14 people who are actively subscribed. Likely a normal targeting reason, but not confirmed yet — worth a 5-minute look.
whats_changed: A new version of the website went live between yesterday and today, and every single check performed on it today came back clean — no errors, correct page loads, all fixes holding.

A long-open question was resolved: the newsletter subscriber who never showed a delivery confirmation had simply unsubscribed on their own a few days after the email went out — not a technical delivery failure. The most recent newsletter send (Sept 6) delivered cleanly to all 8 of its recipients.
The state-named-destination-pages issue found two days ago is still not fixed — re-tested directly today and confirmed unchanged. Low real-world impact, as before.
New and minor: the most recent newsletter send reached fewer subscribers than the total actively-subscribed list — flagged for a quick check, likely benign.
risks: The recurring daily housekeeping gap (saving report files to the project's permanent history) showed up again today, in a smaller way than before — worth a permanent fix so it stops needing to be caught by hand each day.

A background job that keeps hotel/stay recommendations current still can't fully double-check its own work due to a technical network restriction in its automated environment — it has a reliable backup check in place (and even caught two content-quality issues on its own today), but a permanent fix would remove the need for that workaround.

The wrong-response-code issue on state-named destination pages remains unfixed after being found 2 days ago — still low priority, but it's been open for 2 checks now without a developer picking it up.
bottom_line: No urgent action needed on the site itself today — a fresh update went out and everything checked came back completely healthy.
Good news to close the books on: the newsletter delivery mystery from over a week ago is solved and was never a bug.

Still worth a developer's time when convenient: the wrong-response-code issue on 5 state-named destination pages (Puducherry, Goa, Sikkim, Delhi, Chandigarh) — unchanged since it was found 2 days ago.
Worth 5 minutes: check why the last newsletter send reached 8 of 14 active subscribers rather than all of them.
Worth a slightly more serious look: the background report-saving gap keeps recurring in different shapes — tracing the automated job's log directly would likely resolve it once and for all.
tomorrow: Tomorrow's check will re-confirm today's fixes are still holding after the new website update, sample a fresh 10 random destinations, and check whether the newsletter send-reach question got resolved.
It will also take a fresh look at whether the state-named-destination-pages issue has had any developer attention yet, since it's now been open for 2 consecutive checks.

business_about_this_report.note: How this report gets made, for context:
items: This check runs on a daily schedule without anyone needing to trigger it by hand. It visits the live site the same way a real visitor would — loading pages, following links, and reading what actually comes back — rather than just checking that the underlying code looks correct.

Every number in this report comes from something measured today: a page that was actually loaded, a database query that was actually run, or a screen that was actually looked at. Nothing here is estimated or copied forward from a previous day without being re-checked.

Three versions of this report are produced from the same underlying checks: this plain-language version for a business owner, a more detailed version for whoever is doing QA review, and a fully technical version for whoever is fixing things day-to-day.

When something can't be checked for a good reason (for example, a check that would require submitting a real form, or a deeper review that's simply not due yet), that's stated plainly rather than skipped silently or guessed at.

This report and the two more technical companion reports are all regenerated from a single underlying set of today's results — none of the three re-runs any checks or re-measures anything independently.
If a number in this report looks surprising, the more detailed companion reports break every section down further, section by section, with the specific evidence behind each pass or fail.
